name: Is spray painting or roller painting better for a vacant foreclosed property?

mainEntity.name: Is spray painting or roller painting better for a vacant foreclosed property?

acceptedAnswer.text: A spray application combined with back-rolling is usually the best approach for foreclosed homes undergoing complete rehabilitation. When a vacant house is completely empty, professional airless spraying covers large expanses of walls, ceilings, and closet interiors rapidly and cost-effectively. Back-rolling immediately after spraying pushes the paint into the drywall pores and texture, providing superior adhesion and making future touch-ups easier. For occupied flips or projects where new flooring and cabinetry are already installed, traditional hand-rolling and brush cutting protect finished surfaces from overspray.
acceptedAnswer.description: Spraying paired with back-rolling is the most efficient and thorough method for empty foreclosures, while hand-rolling is best if finished floors or cabinets are already in place.
